tool_name: ServiceNow Enterprise Agile Planning (EAP) — part of ServiceNow Strategic Portfolio Management (SPM Pro), delivered on the Strategic Planning Workspace (SPW). Vendor: ServiceNow, Inc.
target_user: Primarily ServiceNow platform admins (scrum_admin / sn_apw_advanced.eap_user / sn_safe.admin) plus SPM implementation partners. Release Train Engineers, Portfolio Managers, and Product Managers consume the system but cannot stand it up themselves — initial configuration is admin-gated, not self-service for team leads or individual contributors.
setup_time_estimate: Typical end-to-end ServiceNow implementation timelines run 3–8+ months, with G2 review data citing an average of ~5 months for SPM-class deployments. Standing up EAP specifically (ARTs, planning calendars, sprint calendars, planning intervals, team integration settings, ACLs, Jira/ADO connectors) is commonly measured in multiple weeks of admin effort even on top of an existing SPM instance. [uncertain] No vendor-published 'time to first PI running' benchmark exists; estimate based on ServiceNow Community threads, partner implementation guides, and G2/Gartner review commentary.
onboarding_wizard: There is no single onboarding wizard. ServiceNow ships a 'Quick Start Guide for Enterprise Agile Planning in SPM' (Community article) and a Guided Setup for SAFe→EAP migration, plus a Guided Setup for the EAP↔Jira integration (Dec 2025 store release). These are sequenced task lists inside the platform rather than a Linear/Notion-style first-run wizard. Branching is by topology (Essential SAFe vs. Portfolio SAFe; EAP standalone vs. EAP+Jira vs. EAP+Azure DevOps) and must be chosen by the admin up front.
template_library: EAP ships with SAFe-aligned configurations (Essential SAFe and Portfolio SAFe) and OOTB record types (EAP Epic, EAP Feature, EAP Story, ART, Planning Interval, Sprint Calendar). Demand-to-EAP conversion templates exist for Epic/Feature. There is no Linear/ClickUp-style gallery of pre-built boards or sprint templates that a team lead can pick from at setup — templates are platform-level artifacts, not user-facing onboarding choices. [uncertain] Cross-team template publishing/sharing is admin-driven via Update Sets and scoped apps rather than an in-product 'publish template' action.
ai_assisted_setup: Now Assist for SPM (generative AI add-on) provides AI for runtime activities — generating user stories from epics, summarizing demands/feedback, drafting project summary emails, monitoring critical path changes via AI agents, and conversational demand creation. None of these target initial EAP configuration: AI does not auto-suggest an ART topology, infer team boundaries from a connected Jira/GitHub, generate a planning calendar, or pre-populate workflow states. Now Assist must itself be licensed and configured by an admin before any of these features are available.
hierarchy_config: Fixed SAFe hierarchy: Portfolio → Solution Train → Agile Release Train (ART) → Team, with work item levels Epic → Capability → Feature → Story. The structure is opinionated and reflects SAFe — flexibility comes from choosing Essential SAFe (no Solution Train layer) vs. Portfolio SAFe. Setting up the hierarchy requires creating ART records, linking SAFe ARTs to EAP ARTs, defining Solution Trains where applicable, creating teams under each ART, then linking Team Integration Settings before any Planning Interval can be created. Each layer is a separate admin task; there is no 'create my org in one screen' flow.
multi_team_setup: Scaling from 1 ART to many is largely a repeat-the-config exercise. Each ART requires its own planning calendar, sprint calendar spans, planning intervals, team list, and Team Integration Settings. There is no bulk-onboard-N-teams action and no self-service ART creation for a Release Train Engineer — net new ARTs and Solution Trains are admin tasks. At enterprise scale (10s–100s of ARTs) customers typically rely on a ServiceNow implementation partner, Update Sets, and scripted CMDB/HR-feed integrations to provision team structures.
admin_dependency: Heavy. Admin-only tasks include: installing/upgrading the EAP and Now Assist plugins, creating planning calendars, creating sprint calendar spans, creating Planning Intervals, configuring SAFe vs. EAP ART linkage, configuring Team Integration Settings for Jira/ADO, creating ACLs on EAP Epic/Feature/Capability tables, configuring Demand-to-EAP conversion, and granting roles (scrum_admin, sn_apw_advanced.eap_user, sn_safe.admin). Team leads can manage their backlog, sprint, and team members once provisioned, but cannot create their own ART, planning interval, or integration. The self-service boundary effectively sits at the Team level inside an already-provisioned ART.
permissions_model: Role-based with extensive ACLs. Key roles include scrum_admin (full Agile Development 2.0 access), scrum_master, scrum_user, sn_apw_advanced.eap_user (required for EAP Team creation from Demand), and sn_safe.admin. ACLs are configured per-table and per-operation (read/write/create/delete), which gives precise control but is non-trivial to configure correctly. Reviewers consistently describe ServiceNow's permission/ACL model as powerful but complex — 'tailoring workflows typically requires skilled admins' (G2). Wrong ACL setup commonly blocks team-level adoption while teams wait for enterprise config.
import_capabilities: EAP supports bi-directional integration (not bulk one-shot import) with Jira (OOTB Guided Setup as of Dec 2025 store release) and Azure DevOps (via the EAP↔ADO connector, with a separate path for ADO teams integrated through legacy SAFe). There is no first-party CSV import wizard at the EAP/ART/PI level comparable to Linear's importer. Migration from competing tools (Rally, VersionOne, Targetprocess) typically goes through ServiceNow Professional Services or a partner-built migration utility. Field mapping for the Jira connector is configurable but requires admin setup of Team Integration Settings per team.
migration_story: The most documented migration path is the internal one: legacy ServiceNow SAFe → EAP. ServiceNow ships a 'SAFe Migration Guided Setup' (Yokohama docs) because the previous SAFe application is deprecated with the Zurich release (Fall 2025). Community threads describe this as a multi-step, admin-led process: verify EAP configuration, run the guided migration tool, validate data, then cut over. For external migrations (e.g. Jira→EAP at scale, Rally→EAP), customers typically engage ServiceNow Professional Services or an implementation partner; this is not a self-service experience. Reviewer commentary: 'initial setup was very difficult due to partner firm not knowing how to implement it.'
vcs_integration_setup: There is no first-party EAP↔GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket connector at parity with Linear's GitHub app. VCS linkage typically flows through ServiceNow DevOps (a separate SKU) or through the Jira/ADO integration where the actual GitHub PR links live in Jira or ADO. Setup therefore requires (1) standing up Jira or ADO integration, then (2) configuring the underlying VCS connection inside that tool. Time-to-first-linked-PR end-to-end is measured in days of admin work, not minutes. [uncertain] First-party VCS support for EAP may exist in later release trains beyond Zurich; not confirmed in current docs.
slack_notifications_setup: ServiceNow provides a Slack integration at the platform level (via the Now Platform Slack app and the Workplace Service Delivery suite) and supports MS Teams. Configuration is platform-admin-driven: install the connector, configure OAuth/app credentials, then map EAP record events to Slack channels via Flow Designer or notification rules. Individual team members generally cannot wire 'notify my channel when this story changes status' without admin help, in contrast to Linear's per-user/per-team Slack settings. [uncertain] Out-of-the-box EAP-event templates for Slack are not prominently documented; most customers build these in Flow Designer.
first_impression_ux: On day 1 the user lands inside the Strategic Planning Workspace (SPW) — a polished workspace UI introduced for SPM Pro. If the admin has not yet provisioned ARTs, Planning Intervals, and Team Integration Settings, the experience is largely empty or shows only seed records. There is no sample ART, no demo PI, no curated walkthrough of 'here is your first sprint board.' Gartner reviewers describe the broader SPM tool as feature-rich but 'not as user-friendly to handle.' Day-1 perception is heavily mediated by how much an admin or partner pre-configured before user access was granted.
time_to_value: Time-to-value is long. A team only feels productive once their ART, Planning Interval, sprint calendar, Team Integration Settings, and (typically) Jira/ADO integration are all live — meaning value lags admin setup by weeks. There is no public-facing free tier or trial that demonstrates EAP value before procurement; EAP requires SPM Pro licensing on a ServiceNow instance. The de facto 'minimum viable setup' is: one ART, one Planning Interval with sprint calendar spans loaded, at least one team with integration settings, and roles granted — still a multi-day admin sequence at best.
setup_complaints: Recurring complaints across Gartner Peer Insights and G2 reviews of ServiceNow SPM/EAP: (1) 'Deployments are often lengthy and may take months to fully configure.' (2) 'Initial setup was very difficult due to partner firm not knowing how to implement it.' (3) 'Tailoring workflows typically requires skilled admins and can be resource-intensive.' (4) 'Initial setup and customization can be complex, especially without experienced admins.' (5) Community threads flag Planning Calendars, CWM linkage, and dashboards as 'not the easiest to configure,' and users report confusion over the Planning Interval / Sprint Calendar / ART linkage prerequisites. (6) Hidden costs cited: partner hours, internal admin time, workflow redesign, upgrade testing, training, data cleanup, ongoing customization maintenance.
setup_praise: Where reviewers do praise ServiceNow EAP setup, it is usually about end-state breadth, not setup ease: 'a smooth experience that ensures investments, portfolios, and projects are directly linked to business growth,' 'easy integrations and day-to-day workflows that reduce manual work,' and the value of consolidating onto the Now Platform alongside ITSM, HRSD, and SecOps. The unified data model is repeatedly cited as the payoff that justifies the setup cost. Gartner overall rating: 4.2/5 across 81 reviews in the EAP Tools market (as of the Gartner Peer Insights pages indexed in this research).
standout_setup_feature: The Guided Setup framework, applied to two specific journeys: (1) SAFe→EAP migration (the only credible in-product path away from the deprecated SAFe app), and (2) EAP↔Jira integration (Dec 2025 store release, OOTB). These are differentiated because they are tied to ServiceNow's unique problem space — legacy SAFe customers and large enterprises that have to keep Jira running alongside EAP. They are not differentiated as 'easy onboarding' moments in the Linear/Monday sense; they are differentiated as 'we acknowledge how painful this migration is and provide a structured path.'
servicenow_comparison: This is ServiceNow EAP itself — it is the baseline that other tools in this research are compared against. Sentiment summary versus modern dev-first tools (Linear, Shortcut, Height): EAP wins on enterprise breadth, SAFe alignment, unified Now Platform data model, and portfolio-to-team traceability; loses on setup time, admin dependency, self-service onboarding, and time-to-first-value. Against Atlassian (Jira + Jira Align): Gartner peer comparisons show competitive feature parity at the enterprise tier but ServiceNow is generally perceived as more admin-heavy at initial setup, while Jira Align carries a similar reputation for implementation complexity.
